vulnerability.title: Ensure All User Initialization Files Have Mode 0740 Or Less Permissive
vulnerability.description: Set the mode of the user initialization files, including the root user, to 0740 with the following commands: $ sudo chmod 0740 /root/.INIT_FILE $ sudo chmod 0740 /home/USER/.INIT_FILE
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: var_user_initialization_files_regex='' readarray -t interactive_users < <(awk -F: '$3==0 || $3>=1000 {print $1}' /etc/passwd) readarray -t interactive_users_home < <(awk -F: '$3==0 || $3>=1000 {print $6}' /etc/passwd) readarray -t interactive_users_shell < <(awk -F: '$3==0 || $3>=1000 {print $7}' /etc/passwd) USERS_IGNORED_REGEX='nobody|nfsnobody' for (( i=0; i<"${#interactive_users[@]}"; i++ )); do if ! grep -qP "$USERS_IGNORED_REGEX" <<< "${interactive_users[$i]}" && \ [ "${interactive_users_shell[$i]}" != "/sbin/nologin" ]; then readarray -t init_files < <(find "${interactive_users_home[$i]}" -maxdepth 1 \ -exec basename {} \; | grep -P "$var_user_initialization_files_regex") for file in "${init_files[@]}"; do chmod u-s,g-wxs,o= "${interactive_users_home[$i]}/$file" done fi done

triage_decision.reason: Changing permissions of user initialization files to 0740 is a standard STIG hardening step that does not risk lockout or critical service disruption.
triage_decision.estimated_impact: authentication/authorization affected; filesystems affected; Potential mis‑application could affect user startup scripts, but unlikely to break authentication or services

        done

done

previous_review_verdicts.feedback: The proposed plan will set the permissions of standard shell initialization files to 0740 and should effectively address the vulnerability.  It is simple, idempotent, and unlikely to introduce lockout or service disruption.
concerns: The `-maxdepth 2` may match files in nested subdirectories that are not intended for initialization scripts; consider using `-maxdepth 1` to target only home directories.  The command does not explicitly exclude non-interactive users (e.g., services) but matching by file name should mitigate that issue.  It does not account for custom init file names that may be required in the environment, though those are outside the scope of the standard STIG requirement.
suggested_improvements: Use `-maxdepth 1` instead of 2 to avoid changing files in subdirectories.  Add a quick check to ensure root’s home directory contains the files before attempting to chmod.  Optionally log the files modified for audit purposes.  If the environment uses additional init files beyond the standard list, extend the `-name` list accordingly.  Consider running the command with `sudo` or as root if the script is not already executed with sufficient privileges.
